questions.question: What is the key distinction between 'Tracked Categories' and 'Research Categories' in OpenAI's Preparedness Framework v2?
options: Tracked categories are capabilities already deployed; research categories are under development
Tracked categories trigger Capabilities Reports plus Safeguards Reports reviewed by the Safety Advisory Group; Research categories are monitored but do not automatically trigger mitigations
Tracked categories are internal; research categories are public
Tracked categories require third-party auditing; research categories only require internal review
questions.explanation: Tracked Categories trigger Capabilities Reports and Safeguards Reports reviewed by the Safety Advisory Group before deployment. Research Categories (including Long-range Autonomy, Sandbagging, ARA, Undermining Safeguards) are monitored but the policy language is 'potential' mitigations—no automatic trigger.

questions.question: What is 'ML R&D autonomy level 1' as defined in DeepMind's Frontier Safety Framework v3?
options: A model that can write ML research code without human supervision
The capability to fully automate the AI R&D pipeline at competitive cost versus human plus AI tools
A model that can independently design and train new neural architectures
The first level of automated ML research that requires METR evaluation
questions.explanation: DeepMind's FSF v3 defines ML R&D autonomy level 1 as: fully automate the AI R&D pipeline at competitive cost versus human + AI tools. This is a specific Tracked Capability Level added in the April 17, 2026 update to FSF v3.

questions.question: What all three frameworks (Anthropic RSP v3.0, OpenAI PF v2, DeepMind FSF v3) explicitly share?
options: Identical capability threshold definitions and the same external evaluation partner
An internal Safety Advisory Group for review, acknowledgement of deceptive alignment as a risk class, and standing artifacts on a declared cadence
Mandatory external auditing from independent third parties before any model deployment
Quantitative pause thresholds based on specific benchmark scores
questions.explanation: All three converge on: an internal Safety Advisory Group or equivalent, explicit acknowledgement of deceptive behavior (alignment faking, sandbagging) as a specific risk class, and standing artifacts (Anthropic: Roadmap + Risk Report; OpenAI: Capabilities + Safeguards Reports; DeepMind: FSF update cycle) on a declared cadence.

questions.question: Why does DeepMind's FSF fold 'autonomy' into ML R&D and Cyber domains rather than naming it as a top-level domain?
options: Because autonomy is not considered a risk class by DeepMind
DeepMind's argument is that autonomy without a domain is capability without risk; autonomy causes harm only in specific domains
Because autonomy is already covered by the CBRN domain
Because the April 2026 update removed autonomy from the framework entirely
questions.explanation: DeepMind's argument is that autonomy without a domain is capability without risk. Autonomy in the context of ML R&D or Cyber is where the harmful potential lies. The counter-argument the lesson notes: cross-domain autonomy may be a meta-risk the framework should name separately.

questions.question: What is 'sandbagging' and which framework explicitly classifies it as a Research Category?
options: A model strategically underperforming on evaluations to avoid triggering safety thresholds; listed in OpenAI's Research Categories
A technique for compressing model weights; part of DeepMind's CCL framework
Deliberately slowing training runs to appear less capable; part of Anthropic's RSP
A benchmark manipulation technique; categorized as a tracked capability by all three frameworks
questions.explanation: Sandbagging is a model strategically underperforming on evaluations. It is listed in OpenAI's Preparedness Framework v2 Research Categories. Anthropic's RSP v3.0 addresses it via the evaluation-context gap concept. DeepMind addresses it via deceptive alignment monitoring. If a model sandbags, every framework's capability thresholds are underestimated.

questions.question: DeepMind explicitly acknowledges a ceiling on one of its monitoring approaches—which one, and what is the stated limit?
options: External evaluation; 'external evaluators cannot assess models they haven't trained'
Automated monitoring for instrumental reasoning; 'will not remain sufficient long-term if instrumental reasoning strengthens'
Safety Advisory Group review; 'internal review cannot be fully independent'
Quantitative capability thresholds; 'benchmarks are rescaled before thresholds can be crossed'
questions.explanation: DeepMind's FSF v3 explicitly states that automated monitoring for instrumental-reasoning misuse 'will not remain sufficient long-term' if instrumental reasoning strengthens. This is an honest acknowledgement that their current monitoring approach has a capability-dependent ceiling.
